target.name: libheif
target.ecosystem: C/C++ image-processing library consumed by applications, packages, and operating-system distributions

disclosure.boundary: Exact-library replay of a public historical finding using pinned vulnerable and fixed revisions.

brief.headline: libheif <= 1.22.0 is vulnerable to a crafted-file out-of-bounds heap read; the defect is fixed in 1.22.1.
brief.confidence: High for the exact vulnerable/fixed decoder-path differential, bounded by the parsed-equivalent harness caveat.

riskAxes.reachability: Requires a crafted HEIF file to be processed by a vulnerable application.
riskAxes.ecosystemImpact: Can crash downstream image-processing applications that accept untrusted HEIF input.

severitySummary: One medium-severity issue affects libheif <= 1.22.0: an integer-wrapped range check can cause a two-byte heap-buffer over-read. Upstream fixed it in 1.22.1; downstream consumers should upgrade or backport and retain regression coverage.

findings.title: CVE-2026-49271: wrapped icef range causes libheif out-of-bounds read

impact.summary: A crafted HEIF input can crash a vulnerable consuming process.

reachability.preconditions: A vulnerable application processes the supplied HEIF input; user interaction is required.

rootCause.failure: integer wrap before the range decision

steps: Build vulnerable commit `b12b733d1716595483413ccd7e2dfb73c44a8d69` with AddressSanitizer and the uncompressed codec enabled.
Run the pinned parsed-equivalent cmpC/icef harness and observe `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 2`.
Confirm the failing frame resolves to `libheif/codecs/uncompressed/unc_decoder.cc:178`.
Run the same harness against exact fix `5782bca04a70ebc01c59397205a3cfff22841311`; confirm `returned error? 1 output=0` and no sanitizer marker.

sections.heading: F-22 — Impact
sections.prose: libheif <= 1.22.0 can read past a heap buffer while decoding a crafted HEIF uncompressed item. In applications that accept untrusted HEIF files, the fault can terminate the process and interrupt image-processing workflows. The published 6.5 medium score reflects high availability impact without evidence of confidentiality or integrity impact.

sections.heading: F-22 — Affected range and root cause
sections.prose: At `libheif/codecs/uncompressed/unc_decoder.cc:178`, the vulnerable range check evaluates `unit_offset + unit_size` without first preventing integer wrap. A wrapped sum can pass the bounds decision and drive a two-byte read outside heap storage.

sections.heading: F-22 — Vulnerable/fixed differential
sections.prose: At vulnerable commit `b12b733d1716595483413ccd7e2dfb73c44a8d69`, the parsed-equivalent harness produces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow`, `READ of size 2`, and `libheif/codecs/uncompressed/unc_decoder.cc:178`. At exact fix `5782bca04a70ebc01c59397205a3cfff22841311`, the same harness returns `returned error? 1 output=0` and remains sanitizer-clean.

sections.heading: F-22 — Fix and downstream action
sections.prose: Upstream fixed the defect in `5782bca04a70ebc01c59397205a3cfff22841311`, released in libheif 1.22.1. Downstream maintainers should upgrade to 1.22.1 or later or backport the exact fix, retain the differential sanitizer case as a regression test, map packages and products still carrying libheif <= 1.22.0, and align advisories with deployed backports.

sections.heading: F-22 — Evidence provenance
sections.prose: Public source binding: `GHSA-r7qj-cg5r-r6vf` / `CVE-2026-49271`, vulnerable commit `b12b733d1716595483413ccd7e2dfb73c44a8d69`, and exact fix `5782bca04a70ebc01c59397205a3cfff22841311`. Claim mode: public historical reproduction; rediscovery: false.

code_differential.commit: unci: prevent integer overflow when reading compressed data (GHSA-r7qj-cg5r-r6vf)

findings.what_it_is: While decoding a crafted HEIF uncompressed item, libheif validates the compressed-data slice with a range check that adds two attacker-influenced values (unit_offset + unit_size) before comparing against the buffer size. On a wrapped sum the check passes and the decoder performs a two-byte read past the end of heap-allocated compressed_bytes storage.
findings.engineering_distinction: A textbook integer-overflow-before-bounds-check: the additive form of the guard is the defect, not a missing guard. HIGH availability, NONE confidentiality/integrity — the primitive is a bounded two-byte over-read that crashes the consuming process, so it caps at 6.5 medium rather than escalating to memory disclosure or code execution. The fix is not a new check but a re-expression of the same check in subtraction form that cannot wrap.

globalSections.heading: Evidence boundary
globalSections.prose: The harness constructs parsed-equivalent cmpC/icef decoder objects and exercises the exact vulnerable library path; it is not a complete malicious .heif parsed through the public decoder API. The differential establishes behavior at the pinned vulnerable and fixed revisions; it does not extend the claim beyond that tested decoder path.

business.bottomLine: libheif <= 1.22.0 can crash while processing a crafted HEIF input; 1.22.1 contains the fix. Downstream projects should upgrade or backport and map products that still accept untrusted HEIF files through an affected version.
